messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 35-year-old man presents to the physician for a medical evaluation necessary before joining the armed force services. He is a healthy man with no history of smoking or substance abuse. His past medical history is not significant. His vital signs are stable and his systemic examination is within normal limits. Examination of his respiratory system, including auscultation of his chest, does not reveal any abnormality. His laboratory investigations are within normal limits but his chest radiogram shows a solitary pulmonary nodule (SPN), size 9 mm (0.35 in) in diameter, in the middle zone of his right lung. The physician compares the radiogram with a radiogram obtained 3 years back for pre-employment medical evaluation. The physician notes that a similar SPN with the same size was present in the previous radiogram at the same location. Which of the following is the next best step in his evaluation?

Options:
A. No further workup
B. Thin-section computed tomography (CT) scan
C. Positron emission tomography (PET) scan
D. Follow-up after 12 months; if unchanged, no further follow-up
E. Follow-up every 6 months; CT scan when there are changes in the nodule

Correct answer: A. No further workup

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is a pulmonary medicine question about evaluating a stable solitary pulmonary nodule on chest imaging, with no psychiatric content."}
